title: Ownership of an unmarked spur on a compact route
question: Trace the thick dark network from the green start. Does the path to the amber terminal contain an extra unmarked dead-end spur? Ignore the colored terminal markers; answer yes or no.

task_signature.mechanism: Recover the one connected thick route network, orient its fork from the green start, and determine whether the unmarked degree-one side branch is attached to the amber-directed arm.

latent_z.description: A compact, randomly translated and oriented thick fork has one unmarked dead-end spur attached to either the amber or violet arm; remote gray ornaments are nondiagnostic and an order-only alias is tested.

latent_alias.justification: The renderer draws two identical gray ornaments in a commutative draw-order loop, so swapping the latent decor_order list is a nontrivial pixel-identical alias and leaves the spur-terminal gold unchanged.

boundary.observable: The amber and violet arms have a large, visible separation from the single extra dark spur; the answer changes when the spur-bearing arm is exchanged, while terminal colors and positions are independently balanced.
boundary.quarantine: Quarantine if the dark component, colored marker, fork, or spur cannot be recovered with stable pixel margins, including any touching or near-touching marker or skeleton ambiguity.

semantic_contrast.contrast: Those worlds ask for loop existence, bridge indispensability, filled-area mass, directed tangent binding, or geodesic distance. This candidate instead identifies an uncolored degree-one side branch and binds its attachment to one colored arm; it has no cycle, marked cut edge, length ranking, bend count, or checkpoint-order decision.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: It isolates whether a model can parse local route topology and assign an anonymous dead-end branch to a colored terminal path from the raster alone.
